notes: Python import resolution: a stdlib import (os) with no scanned match is external; absolute dotted imports resolve to the scanned package file. `from pkg.mod_b import b` reaches the resolver as `pkg.mod_b.b` (the analyzer folds the imported name into the path), so the trailing symbol segment is trimmed until a module matches. NOTE: relative imports (from . import x) still arrive without their dot level (analyzer limitation) and resolve against the importing file's own package only — never repo-wide — so a miss is Unresolved, never a wrong file.
Transitive importers of pkg/mod_b.py: mod_a.py imports it (from pkg import mod_b), and main.py imports mod_a, so both are in the reverse closure.
